About Analog Devices

Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.

          

About the Role 

As an Associate Embedded Software Engineer, you will contribute to the development of embedded software solutions that power Analog Devices' innovative products and technologies. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will participate in the design, implementation, testing, and support of software that interfaces with hardware systems and enables product functionality. 

Key Responsibilities 

Develop, maintain, and debug embedded software and firmware components under the guidance of experienced engineers. 
Participate in software development activities including coding, testing, debugging, and documentation. 
Assist in integrating software with hardware systems and embedded platforms. 
Support software verification, validation, and troubleshooting efforts throughout the development cycle. 
Collaborate with cross-functional teams including hardware, systems, applications, and product engineering teams. 
Contribute to technical documentation, software design discussions, and code reviews. 
Apply software engineering principles and development best practices to assigned tasks. 

Must Have Skills 

Knowledge of software development fundamentals and programming concepts. 
Experience with C and/or C++ programming through coursework, projects, internships, or professional experience. 
Understanding of embedded systems concepts, microcontrollers, or hardware-software interaction. 
Familiarity with debugging tools and problem-solving techniques. 
Exposure to version control systems such as Git or similar tools. 
Strong analytical, communication, and teamwork skills. 

Preferred Education and Experience 

Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. 
0-2 years of relevant experience in embedded software development, firmware development, or related engineering disciplines. 
Exposure to firmware, embedded software, or low-level programming projects. 
Familiarity with software testing, validation, or debugging methodologies. 
Experience working with embedded development tools, IDEs, or compilers. 
Academic, internship, or personal project experience involving embedded systems, electronics, or software-hardware integration. 
Knowledge of scripting languages such as Python or Shell scripting. 

For positions requiring access to technical data, Analog Devices, Inc. may have to obtain export  licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce - Bureau of Industry and Security and/or the U.S. Department of State - Directorate of Defense Trade Controls.  As such, applicants for this position – except US Citizens, US Permanent Residents, and protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) – may have to go through an export licensing review process.

The expected wage range for a new hire into this position is $71,989 to $99,006.

Actual wage offered may vary depending on work location, experience, education, training, external market data, internal pay equity, or other bona fide factors.
